precepts.text: The people sinned against the Lord in eating with the blood; Saul had every man slay his beast on the great stone so they sinned not.
precepts.point: Serve the Lord and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, and take sickness away from the midst of thee: keep the dietary laws, what to eat and not eat, how to cook it and how to season it, and do not bow down to the gods of the heathen nor do after their works.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
Israel fell into this sin in Saul’s day. “Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.” The people had flown upon the spoil and eaten with the blood, and Saul called it what it was: transgression.

Saul had every man bring his ox and his sheep and slay them on the great stone, “and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood.” Eating with the blood is sin.

That is why you make sure your food is thoroughly cooked, well done, cut open to the bone so it cooks through. Meat served rare is not running with juice, it is blood.

precepts.text: Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one to deliver with a great multitude or a small company; we do not have to come deep to get the victory.
precepts.point: The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Between the passages were two sharp rocks, Bozez and Seneh, one facing Michmash and the other Gibeah. Jonathan said, “Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.” The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan.

Judas answered in the same spirit: “It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: For the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven.” We do not have to come deep to get the victory.

That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

precepts.text: Asa cried unto the Lord, It is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude; that is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant, two men going against an army in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Asa had the same faith: “Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.”

That is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant: “there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.” Two men going against an army in the name of the Lord.

precepts.text: My son, fear thou the Lord and the king, and meddle not with them that are given to change; Saul was the king and put out an order, and when someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next.
precepts.point: Jonathan said, My father hath troubled the land: see how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey; how much more, if haply the people had eaten freely of the spoil of their enemies, had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines? He began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king's order was folly.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Jonathan had not heard his father charge the people with the oath. He dipped the end of his rod in an honeycomb, “and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.” Like the first taste after a long fast, he felt like a whole new creature. Then he was told, “Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.”

Jonathan answered, “My father hath troubled the land”, and began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king’s order was folly: “How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?”

“My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change”. Saul was the king and put out an order. When someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next.

precepts.text: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me; somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul.
precepts.point: If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Saul proposed, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light”, and the people agreed. Then the priest said, “Let us draw near hither unto God.” Saul asked, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.”

“If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me”. Somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul. If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

precepts.text: Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear; sin and iniquity are what cause the Most High not to hear you, plain and clear.
precepts.point: If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” Sin and iniquity are what cause the Most High not to hear you, plain and clear.

So when Saul asked counsel of God and “he answered him not that day”, the silence was the answer: iniquity had separated them from their God.

precepts.text: He shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell.
precepts.point: In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
The people stood up for Jonathan: “Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.” They kept him from the wrath of his father.

Think about the contrast, and why the scripture says to get the love of the congregation. In chapter 13 Saul was the one disobeying the voice of the Lord and getting rebuked, while Jonathan was brave and mighty and had just saved Israel out of the hand of its enemies. Now the coward wants to kill the deliverer.

“For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.” Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell. In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives.
